findings.title: isSidebarThreadWorking re-export is now test-only
findings.body: Sidebar.tsx no longer imports `isSidebarThreadWorking`, and the only remaining references are the re-export at `apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.logic.ts:970` and `Sidebar.logic.test.ts`. If knip does not count test imports as usage, `vp run check:changed` will flag it as an unused export. If it does not, the alias can stay. Check which applies and drop the alias if knip flags it.

findings.title: Interrupted/cancelled/rolled_back test only checks the hold, not that the grace expires
findings.body: The `it.each(["interrupted","cancelled","rolled_back"])` test asserts `isWorking` is true right after the stop, then ends the hold by setting `settledOverride`. It never advances the timers, so it doesn't show these statuses still leave the Working shelf after 2s. The `actionable` check in `threadInbox.ts:198-205` excludes only `failed` runs, and the other tests cover expiry only for `completed`. Add `vi.advanceTimersByTime(WORKING_EXIT_GRACE_MS)` and assert `isWorking` is false.

contracts.action: Thread-triggered settlement sweeps now run as one fiber per thread, off the full-sweep worker
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous single `makeDrainableWorker` that ran both full and per-thread sweeps in order. It is still used for `fullSweeps` at :534.
contracts.before_after: Before: a thread's stop event waited behind any running full sweep or another thread's host reads. After: `enqueueThread` marks the thread queued, runs `sweepThread` in a FiberSet under an 8-permit semaphore, and records one `rerun` if more events arrive while it runs. `drain` waits for both the full-sweep worker and the FiberSet.
contracts.visible_effect: A thread whose background work or run has ended settles within about the Working shelf's 2s grace, instead of appearing in the inbox and then vanishing.
contracts.failure_mode: `runSweep` catches non-interrupt causes and logs them, so a failed sweep leaves no stuck state. The per-thread sweep can now run at the same time as a full sweep for the same thread, and both can reach `thread.auto-settle`. That dispatch carries `snapshotAt: thread.updatedAt`, so I took it to be guarded against stale snapshots, but I did not read the Orchestrator handler to confirm.

contracts.action: Read open pull request links fresh as soon as an agent's merge/close command ends, and again at run end
contracts.equivalent_path: The `run.updated` terminal branch in the same switch, which calls `refreshOpenLinks`.
contracts.before_after: Before: only a run-end read, triggered by a set of threads that had run a close command. After: a map of thread to command ids. The first ended command (inactive status, id not yet seen) refreshes immediately. The run-end refresh still fires whenever the map has an entry for the thread, so `merge --auto` is read again.
contracts.visible_effect: A thread whose PR was merged by the agent can settle before the run ends. A thread using `merge --auto` is still caught at run end.
contracts.failure_mode: Each close-command run now makes up to two host reads, and the run-end read happens even when the command already refreshed. Map entries are only removed on a terminal run status, as before.

contracts.action: Delay completion notifications by the Working shelf grace through a per-thread gate
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous inline loop in the snapshot effect that notified straight away when the completion timestamp advanced.
contracts.before_after: Before: a completion notified in the same effect pass. After: `createThreadNotificationGate` starts a 2s timer, and any not-settled, archived or quiet observation cancels it. Attention notifies at once and suppresses the earlier pending completion. `present` is an effect event, so the timer reads current settings, focus and route.
contracts.visible_effect: No "Thread completed" toast, sound or desktop notification for an orchestrator run that is followed by a continuation within 2s. Other completions arrive 2s later.
contracts.failure_mode: The gate is created in a mount effect and cleared on unmount, and `previous` is cleared with it, so a StrictMode remount or a switch to `mode === "off"` and back starts fresh and does not replay old completions. `threads === null` clears the gate and `previous`. Threads that leave the snapshot are dropped by `retain`.

contracts.action: Re-render the Sidebar and the mobile list when the Working-exit grace expires
contracts.before_after: Before: the tracker only observed on thread changes, so a held thread stayed in Working until the next unrelated update. After: both clients subscribe to the tracker's version. The Sidebar puts it in `clockKey`, and mobile adds it to the `useMemo` deps that call `observe`. The expiry timer bumps the version and listeners re-render.
contracts.visible_effect: A thread leaves the Working shelf about 2s after it stops, and the row moves to the inbox ordered by the return time.
contracts.failure_mode: The optimistic-drop path calls `inbox(projected, true)`, which uses the raw `isThreadWorking`, so a manual move is never held by the grace.

contracts.action: createInboxReturnTracker.observe now holds a thread that stopped working in the Working shelf for WORKING_EXIT_GRACE_MS (2s) and arms a module-level setTimeout that expires the hold and notifies subscribers
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous observe() stamped a return time the moment a thread stopped working and returned a frozen lookup. Sidebar.tsx:519 and useThreadListV2.ts:62 are the callers.
contracts.before_after: Before: shelf placement followed isThreadWorking directly and the return time was stamped on the first non-working observation. After: states hold working/deadline/placement. Expiry is stamped by the timer or by the next observe, whichever runs first. Grace ends at once on attention requests, failure, archive, delete, pin, settle, snooze or a placement change. The snooze check uses effectiveSnoozed.
contracts.visible_effect: Threads stay in the Working shelf for 2s after finishing, then move to the inbox with a return timestamp. Web re-renders through useSyncExternalStore (Sidebar.tsx:384). Mobile re-observes through useMemo keyed on the version (useThreadListV2.ts:58-66).
contracts.failure_mode: The timer is module-scope and not tied to a component, so it still fires with no subscribers and then only bumps the version. observe(null) and thread removal clear the timer (threadInbox.ts:173-178, 223-229). No rejection path. If the wall clock jumps backwards, a deadline can be pushed later.

contracts.action: What bounds the grace wait: the per-thread deadline and the single rescheduled setTimeout
contracts.before_after: The deadline is set once, at first non-working observation, as at + 2000. It is preserved through later observes via previous.deadline. schedule() arms one timer for the earliest deadline and re-arms after each fire. Resuming work, any exclusion, or removal sets the deadline to null.
contracts.visible_effect: The worst-case hold is 2s after the first observation of the stop. Nothing awaits it, and the user is never blocked.
contracts.failure_mode: The hold cannot extend past the deadline. A repeat observe cannot reset it because previous.deadline is reused.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** I found no defects in this part. The one finding is a "consider": the `isSidebarThreadWorking` re-export in `Sidebar.logic.ts` is now only used by tests, so knip may flag it. I verified the new server sweep, the notification gate, and the Sidebar and mobile grace re-renders by reading the code. I did not run anything, so the new tests are unexecuted.

- **Settlement service:** the per-thread FiberSet and semaphore coalescing is consistent with the full-sweep worker. Two points I could not check by reading. The new `PullRequestSyncReactor` test asserts a single host read, and I did not trace whether the command-end refresh plus the run-end refresh dedupe into one. A per-thread sweep and a full sweep can both dispatch `thread.auto-settle` for the same thread, which I took to be guarded by `snapshotAt`. I did not read the Orchestrator handler.
- **Notification gate:** the first-sighting, archived, quiet, attention and removal cases are handled and match the tests. Remounts are safe because the mount effect clears `previous` along with the gate.
- **Sidebar and mobile:** both clients re-render on grace expiry. Manual drops use the raw `isThreadWorking`, so the grace never applies to them.
- **Judgement call:** completion notifications are now delayed 2s even when the Working shelf beta is off. This is flagged for a maintainer to decide.

**Batch 2 of 2.** I found no defects in the tracker logic. I traced each new test against the implementation with fake timers at t=10_000 and the expected values (12_000, 14_500, 12_500 ordering) hold. Both call sites re-observe when the version changes. One minor test gap: the interrupted/cancelled/rolled_back test never checks that the hold expires.
